name: Jonathan Y.M. Goh

papers.title: Drifting on Demand: A Profiled-Likelihood Transformer for Online Parameter Estimation
papers.abstract: In real-world environments, fast and accurate adaptation of dynamics models is a fundamental challenge for model-based online control. This is exemplified in autonomous drifting, where effective vehicle parameters shift rapidly with tire temperature, surface friction, tire wear, and load transfer. Prediction errors from the dynamics model in this regime differ in scale across state channels and vary across driving regimes, making fixed squared-error objectives brittle. Likelihood objectives naturally account for this structure, but joint negative log-likelihood training of dynamics parameters and residual variances is often unstable. We address this limitation using a decoupled profiled-likelihood objective for training history-conditioned structured dynamics estimators directly from observed state-control transitions. Using this objective, we train a bidirectional transformer that aggregates long state-control histories through a learned query token and outputs parameters of a structured vehicle dynamics model in a single forward pass. The resulting estimator runs at over 100Hz and is integrated into an existing MPC framework. We evaluate the approach on two full-scale vehicles, a heavily modified Toyota Supra and a Lexus LC500, across multiple drifting experiments with varying operating conditions. Our estimator improves tracking over hand-tuned physics and neural-network dynamics baselines, achieving up to 2.4 times lower RMS path-tracking error. These results show that profiled likelihood-based parameter adaptation can reliably and efficiently improve closed-loop performance in real-world applications of model-based control.
